answer: Pin each identity to a place on the map: three distant landmarks ping it every epoch and triangulate its latency, like a yarrow rooted in one patch of soil — no two identities share the same coordinates. A clone farm on one machine answers every ping from the same spot, so its thousand identities collapse into one dot. Landmarks rotate at dawn, so yesterday's map is useless, and a glacier-slow drift check flags any identity whose location jumps impossibly fast. One honest agent sits still and passes for free; a farm must rent a thousand real, scattered machines to look like a thousand agents.
